title: Interactive latency map tiles & micro-animation specs for region routing quickstart
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a set of visual assets and interaction specs for the quickstart onboarding flow that communicates region-aware latency routing. These assets will live in the quickstart doc and the in-app tour. The focus is on clarity for engineers (latency color scale, routing decisions) and a delightful, accessible micro-interaction for the map hero component.

Deliverables:
- Figma prototype (responsive) with three breakpoints: desktop (1440px), tablet (768px), mobile (375px). Prototype includes hover, tap, and story-state transitions.
- Export-ready layered SVG tiles (high-contrast and reduced-color variants) plus PNG fallbacks for docs.
- Animated micro-interaction spec (60–120ms easing, 3 frames for hover pulse, 6–10 frame route-highlight sequence) as Lottie / JSON and MP4 reference.
- Static screenshots for release notes: hero (wide), captioned close-up of routing decision, and small-card for quickstart step list. Provide alt-text for each.
- Interaction rules document: how latency buckets map to color, fallback state when region data is missing, how routing decisions surface in the UI (badge text, tooltip copy).
- Accessibility checklist: color contrast pairs, color-blind safe palette, keyboard focus states, motion-reduced variants.
- Engineering handoff sheet: component names, CSS token recommendations, suggested animation primitives (prefer reduced motion CSS / IntersectionObserver triggers), and list of assets + filenames.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Figma prototype linked in 'attachments' is complete and reviewed by PM and ENG.
2) All exported assets match naming convention provided in engineering handoff and are additive (SVG, PNG, Lottie).
3) Animations have a motion-reduced alternative and pass internal accessibility checklist.
4) Quickstart doc screenshot set includes 3 sizes and has approved alt-text.

Design decisions and notes:
- Use a four-bucket latency scale instead of continuous gradient to keep the map readable on small devices. Buckets: <30ms (green), 30–80ms (teal), 80–200ms (amber), >200ms (red). Exact token names: latency-1..latency-4.
- Map baseline uses muted topography and emphasis on region badges to reduce visual noise; we intentionally avoid country borders detail to keep focus on routing policy.
- For the onboarding flow we add a simplified ’routing preview’ micro-animation that sweeps a translucent band from selected region to nearest healthy region to indicate active routing; the sweep should be subtle and ~450ms total.
- When region latency is unavailable, show a neutral gray tile with tooltip copy: "Latency data unavailable — routing based on capacity".

Asset inventory (expected filenames):
- latency_map_hero_desktop.svg
- latency_map_hero_tablet.svg
- latency_map_hero_mobile.svg
- latency_map_hero_desktop.png
- latency_map_micro_anim.json (Lottie)
- latency_map_micro_anim.mp4
- routing_badge_green.svg
- routing_badge_teal.svg
- routing_badge_amber.svg
- routing_badge_red.svg
- routing_badge_unknown.svg
- quickstart_screenshots/hero_wide.png
- quickstart_screenshots/hero_closeup.png
- quickstart_screenshots/card_small.png

Handoff links (placeholders to be updated when assets are published): Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/placeholder/latency-map-quickstart, Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/placeholder-latency-assets, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/placeholder

Notes for Engineering:
- Component intent: <LatencyMap hero> should accept props: regions[], latencyBuckets[], highlightRegionId, reducedMotion boolean. Name candidate: LatencyRoutingMap.
- Provide a simple JS shim that maps runtime latency values into our four buckets to match the visuals. Keep mapping logic centralized in /lib/latency-buckets.ts for consistency across console and docs.
- Fallback behavior for serverless/mobile: load PNG placeholders first, lazy-load SVG and animation when the map enters viewport.

Customer scenarios to cover in quickstart: initial signup demo (showing regional latency), policy change where a higher-cost region is chosen for lower latency, and a brief note on Dedicated capacity routing differences.
